tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:30
tests.procedure: Under strong white light, check each received container separately in a clean transparent watch glass/dish for foreign particles, colour and conformance. Hygroscopicity: weigh a glass weighing vessel with stopper (m1); add about 2 g substance and weigh (m2); place unstoppered in a climatic cabinet at 25 +/- 1 C for 24 h; stopper and weigh (m3); calculate percentage increase in mass.

hygroscopicity.weighings: m1 vessel+stopper, m2 vessel+sample, m3 after 24 h

details.specification: White or almost white, hygroscopic, crystalline powder
details.reference: BP Monograph for Sodium Methyl Hydroxybenzoate

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:31
tests.procedure: Stepwise solubility (BP descriptive terms) at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C: 100 mg in a stoppered tube + 0.1 mL solvent, shake vigorously 1 min, hold 15 min at 25.0 +/- 0.5 C, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved. Dissolved = very soluble. Not dissolved: add 0.9 mL (freely soluble if dissolved), then 2 mL (soluble), then 7 mL (sparingly soluble), each step shake 1 min + 15 min hold (repeat once). Then 10 mg powdered substance + 10 mL solvent (slightly soluble), then 1 mg + 10 mL (very slightly soluble), otherwise practically insoluble. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent) and methylene chloride.

solvents: water (implied for first pass, not named)
details.specification: Freely soluble in water, sparingly soluble in ethanol (96 per cent), practically insoluble in methylene chloride
details.reference: BP Monograph for Sodium Methyl Hydroxybenzoate

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:32
tests.procedure: Identification test 1 (melting point): dissolve 0.5 g in 50 mL water; immediately add 5 mL hydrochloric acid R1; filter; wash the precipitate with water; dry in vacuo at 80 C for 2 h; determine melting point with a calibrated melting point apparatus. The same precipitate is used for the next identification test.

details.specification: The precipitation melts at 125 C to 128 C
details.reference: BP Appendix V A Determination of Melting Point

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:32; Sodium Methyl Paraben__Specifications sheet Sodium Methyl Paraben.txt:14
tests.procedure: Identification by HPLC retention time (user answer 2026-11-04: the IR wording in the STM and spec sheet is a mistake). Compare the retention time of the major peak of the sample solution with that of the standard solution (Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS or Sodium methyl para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS). The STM text as written describes the precipitate from the melting point test pressed with potassium bromide into a pellet and an IR spectrum compared with the reference; no chromatographic conditions are stated in the identification section.

details.stmWordingIsIR: precipitate from test 1 mixed with KBr, compressed to a transparent pellet, spectrum compared with Methyl/Sodium methyl para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS (BP Appendix II A Infrared Spectrophotometry)
details.standard: Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS, or Sodium Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS
details.specification: The retention time of the major peak of the Sample solution corresponds to that of the Standard solution

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:32
tests.procedure: Identification test 3 (TLC). Test solution (a): 0.10 g in 10 mL water, immediately add 2 mL hydrochloric acid, shake with 50 mL 1,1-dimethylethyl methyl ether, evaporate the upper layer to dryness, take up residue in 10 mL acetone. Test solution (b): dilute 1 mL of (a) to 10 mL with acetone. Reference (a): 10 mg methyl (or sodium methyl) para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS in acetone, dilute to 10 mL. Reference (b): 10 mg ethyl para hydroxybenzoate RS in 1 mL of test solution (a), dilute to 10 mL with acetone. Plate: TLC octadecyl silyl silica gel F254. Mobile phase glacial acetic acid : water : methanol (1:30:70 V/V/V). Apply 5 uL of test solution (b) and references (a) and (b); develop over 2/3 of the plate; dry in air; examine at 254 nm.

testSolutionA.extraction: 50 mL 1,1-dimethylethyl methyl ether, evaporate upper layer, residue in 10 mL acetone

details.testSolutionB: 1 mL of (a) diluted to 10 mL with acetone
details.referenceA: 10 mg methyl para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS or sodium methyl para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS, acetone to 10 mL
details.referenceB: 10 mg ethyl para hydroxybenzoate RS in 1 mL test solution (a), acetone to 10 mL
details.plate: TLC octadecyl silyl silica gel F254
details.mobilePhase: glacial acetic acid : water : methanol (1:30:70 V/V/V)
details.systemSuitability: reference solution (b): chromatogram shows 2 clearly separated principal spots
details.specification: The principal spot in the chromatogram obtained with test solution (b) is similar in position and size to the principal spot in the chromatogram obtained with reference solution (a)
details.reference: BP Appendix III A Thin-layer Chromatography

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:32
tests.procedure: Identification test 4 (reaction of sodium): 1 mL solution S + 1 mL water + 2 mL of 150 g/L potassium carbonate solution, heat to boiling, no precipitate is formed; add 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution, heat to boiling, cool in iced water.

details.intermediateObservation: no precipitate after carbonate and boiling
details.specification: A dense white precipitate is formed
details.reference: BP Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Sodium

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:33; Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:28
tests.procedure: Examine solution S immediately after preparation for clarity and colour against reference solution BY6.

details.solutionS: 5.0 g in carbon dioxide-free water (from distilled water), diluted to 50 mL
details.referenceSolutionBY6: mix 5.0 mL Standard solution BY and 95.0 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L HCl)
details.standardSolutionBY: mix 2.4 mL Yellow solution, 1.0 mL Red solution, 0.4 mL Blue solution and 6.2 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L HCl)
details.yellowSolution: 46 g ferric chloride in about 900 mL of a mixture of 25 mL hydrochloric acid and 975 mL water, dilute to 1000.0 mL with the same mixture
details.redSolution: 60 g cobalt chloride, same diluent, 1000.0 mL
details.blueSolution: 63 g copper sulfate pentahydrate, same diluent, 1000.0 mL
details.specification: Solution S is Clear and not more intensely colored than reference solution BY6
details.reference: BP Appendix IV A Clarity of Solution, Appendix IV B Color of Solution

tests.procedure: Dilute 1 mL of solution S to 100 mL with carbon dioxide-free water; record the pH.

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:35
tests.procedure: HPLC related substances. Test solution: 50.0 mg in 2.5 mL methanol, dilute to 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL with mobile phase. Reference (a): 5 mg 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (impurity A) and 5 mg of the substance in mobile phase to 100.0 mL, then 1.0 mL to 10.0 mL with mobile phase. Reference (b): 50.0 mg methyl (or sodium methyl) para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS in 2.5 mL methanol, 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL. Reference (c): 1.0 mL of test solution to 20.0 mL with mobile phase, then 1.0 mL to 10.0 mL. Inject 10 uL of test solution and references (a) and (c).

column.stationaryPhase: end-capped octadecyl silyl silica gel for chromatography (5 um)

details.mobilePhase: 6.8 g/L solution of potassium dihydrogen phosphate : methanol (35:65 V/V)
details.runTime: 5 times the retention time of methyl para hydroxybenzoate
details.relativeRetention: methyl para hydroxybenzoate about 2.3 min; impurity A about 0.6
details.systemSuitability: reference solution (a): resolution minimum 2.0 between impurity A and methyl para hydroxybenzoate
details.correctionFactor: multiply the peak area of impurity A by 1.4

limits.impurityA: not more than 6 times the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (3.0 per cent)
limits.unspecifiedEach: not more than the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (0.5 per cent)
limits.sumOtherThanA: not more than twice the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (1.0 per cent)
limits.disregardLimit: 0.2 times the area of the principal peak of reference (c) (0.1 per cent)

details.reference: BP Appendix III D Liquid Chromatography

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:36; Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:28
tests.procedure: Limit test, opalescence comparison. Sample: 10 mL solution S + 30 mL water + 1 mL nitric acid, dilute to 50 mL, shake, filter; dilute 10 mL of filtrate to 15 mL with water, add 1 mL dilute nitric acid, pour as a single addition into a test tube containing 1 mL silver nitrate solution R2. Standard: 14 mL chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl) + 1 mL water + 1 mL diluted nitric acid, poured into 1 mL silver nitrate R2. After 5 min protected from light, examine tubes laterally against a black background; opalescence in the test solution not more intense than in the standard.

details.standard: 14 mL chloride standard solution (5 ppm Cl)

reagentPrep.chlorideStandard5ppm: immediately before use dilute with water to 100 times its volume a solution containing sodium chloride equivalent to 0.824 g NaCl in 1000.0 mL
reagentPrep.silverNitrateR2: 1.7 g silver nitrate in water, to 100 mL
reagentPrep.diluteNitricAcid: 20 g nitric acid to 100 mL with water

details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Chlorides

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:37; Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:28
tests.procedure: Limit test, opalescence comparison. Sample: 25 mL solution S + 5 mL distilled water + 10 mL hydrochloric acid, dilute to 50 mL, shake, filter; dilute 10 mL of filtrate to 15 mL with distilled water (solution 1). Add 3 mL of 250 g/L barium chloride to 4.5 mL sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) R1, shake, stand 1 min; to 2.5 mL of this suspension add 15 mL of solution 1 and 0.5 mL acetic acid. Standard: same suspension, 2.5 mL + 15 mL sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) + 0.5 mL acetic acid. After 5 min opalescence in the test solution not more intense than in the standard.

details.standard: 2.5 mL suspension + 15 mL sulfate standard solution (10 ppm SO4) + 0.5 mL acetic acid

reagentPrep.sulfateStandard10ppm: immediately before use dilute with distilled water to 100 times its volume a solution in distilled water containing dipotassium sulfate equivalent to 0.181 g K2SO4 in 100.0 mL

details.reference: BP Appendix VII Limit Tests, Sulfates

tests.source: Sodium Methyl Paraben__Sodium Methyl Paraben- SM.txt:39
tests.procedure: HPLC assay against Methyl or Sodium methyl para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS. Test solution: 50.0 mg in 2.5 mL methanol, dilute to 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL with mobile phase. Standard solution: 50.0 mg of the RS/WS in 2.5 mL methanol, 50.0 mL with mobile phase, then 10.0 mL to 100.0 mL. System suitability: 6 replicate injections of the standard solution. Calculate the content of sodium methylparaben against the declared content of Sodium Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS, or against Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS/WS multiplied by a correction factor of 1.145.

column.stationaryPhase: end-capped octadecyl silyl silica gel for chromatography ODS (5 um)

details.mobilePhase: 6.8 g/L solution of potassium dihydrogen phosphate : methanol (35:65 V/V)
details.relativeRetention: methyl para hydroxybenzoate retention time about 2.3 min
details.systemSuitability: 6 replicate injections of the standard solution (no acceptance limit stated)
details.standards: Sodium Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS (no factor), or Methyl Para hydroxybenzoate RS or WS (multiply by 1.145)
details.formulaAsPrinted: Assay % = PAt/PAst x Act.Wt.std/Theo.Wt.test x 100/(100-MC) x Potency (as printed, terms garbled); PAt = mean area in test, PAst = mean area in standard, MC = moisture content of working standard, Potency = assay of working standard
details.specification: 95.0 per cent to 102.0 per cent (anhydrous substance)
details.reference: BP Appendix III D Liquid Chromatography
